steps.title: Import React, useState, useMemo, and useCallback
steps.instruction: Import React and the hooks useState, useMemo, and useCallback from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement with curly braces to bring in multiple named exports from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React, useState, useMemo, and useCallback here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React hooks for memoization are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React, useState, useMemo, and useCallback are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported all the required hooks for memoization.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but check that you've imported all four: React, useState, useMemo, and useCallback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or incomplete. Please import React, useState, useMemo, and useCallback from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint:
Define a function called App that returns JSX with a single
.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useMemo, useCallback } from 'react';

// Create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns an empty div.
successCriteria: A functional component named App exists and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named App that returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function called App that returns a <div>.

steps.title: Initialize state for counter and input value
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use useState to create two state variables: 'count' initialized to 0 and 'inputValue' initialized to an empty string ''.
steps.hint: Call useState twice: once for count with initial value 0, and once for inputValue with initial value ''.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your App component will have two state variables ready to track the counter and input value.
successCriteria: The App component contains two useState calls: one for count with initial value 0, and one for inputValue with initial value ''.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized both state variables. These will be used to trigger re-renders and demonstrate memoization.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created at least one state variable, but you need both: count (initial 0) and inputValue (initial '').
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've used useState twice inside the App component to create both required state variables.

steps.title: Create a non-memoized expensive calculation function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function named 'expensiveCalculation' that simulates heavy computation by performing a loop that runs 1,000,000 times and returns the result.
steps.hint: Define a regular function (not memoized) that uses a for loop to iterate many times, performing a simple arithmetic operation inside the loop.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function that demonstrates performance issues when called repeatedly without memoization.
successCriteria: The App component contains a function named 'expensiveCalculation' that uses a loop to simulate heavy computation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a function that simulates expensive computation. This will help demonstrate why memoization is needed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named 'expensiveCalculation' and contains a loop that runs many times to simulate heavy computation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Create a function named 'expensiveCalculation' that uses a loop to simulate heavy computation.

steps.title: Create a memoized version with useMemo
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useMemo hook to create a memoizedResult variable that calls expensiveCalculation only when inputValue changes.
steps.hint: Call useMemo with a function that returns expensiveCalculation(inputValue) and pass [inputValue] as the dependency array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A memoizedResult variable is created using useMemo, which will only recalculate when inputValue changes.
successCriteria: useMemo is called with a function that returns expensiveCalculation(inputValue) and has [inputValue] as its dependency array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully memoized the expensive calculation using useMemo. This will prevent unnecessary recalculations when other state values change.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with useMemo. Make sure your function calls expensiveCalculation(inputValue) and includes [inputValue] in the dependency array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try using the useMemo hook to create a memoized version of the expensive calculation. The calculation should only run when inputValue changes.

steps.title: Create event handlers for counter and input
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create two handler functions: one named 'incrementCount' that increments the counter state, and another named 'handleInputChange' that updates the input value state based on the event target's value.
steps.hint: Both handlers should be defined as functions that take the necessary parameters (no parameters for incrementCount, an event for handleInputChange) and call the appropriate state setter functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two handler functions are defined: incrementCount updates the counter state, and handleInputChange updates the input value state based on user input.
successCriteria: The incrementCount function increments the counter state, and handleInputChange updates the input value state using e.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created both event handlers. These functions will allow user interactions to update your component's state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created at least one handler function, but both are needed. Make sure you have incrementCount that increments the counter and handleInputChange that updates the input value from the event.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handlers aren't defined correctly. Remember to create both incrementCount and handleInputChange functions that update their respective state values.

steps.title: Create a non-memoized callback function
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a regular function named 'nonMemoizedCallback' that logs a message to the console when called.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses console.log() to output a message. This function will be recreated on every render.
steps.expectedOutcome: A regular function 'nonMemoizedCallback' is defined inside the App component that logs a message when called.
successCriteria: The App component contains a function named 'nonMemoizedCallback' that calls console.log() with a message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a non-memoized callback function. This function will be recreated on every render, which we'll compare with memoized versions later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named exactly 'nonMemoizedCallback' and includes a console.log() statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a function named 'nonMemoizedCallback' that logs a message using console.log().

steps.title: Create a memoized callback with useCallback
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a memoized callback function named 'memoizedCallback' using the useCallback hook. This function should log a message to the console (e.g., 'Memoized callback executed') and should be memoized based on its dependencies.
steps.hint: Use the useCallback hook you imported earlier. Pass it a function that logs a message, and specify the appropriate dependency array.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a memoized callback function that logs a message and only re-creates when its dependencies change.
successCriteria: The memoizedCallback function is defined using useCallback, logs a message to the console, and has a proper dependency array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a memoized callback using useCallback. This will prevent unnecessary re-creations of the function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the useCallback hook with a function that logs a message and includes the dependency array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to use the useCallback hook to create a memoized function that logs a message.

steps.title: Add the basic JSX structure with headings
steps.instruction: In your App component's return statement, replace 'null' with a JSX fragment containing a main heading and a subheading to explain memoization.
steps.hint: Use a fragment (<>...</>) or a <div> wrapper. Add an <h1> with a title like 'Memoization Demo' and an <h2> with a brief description.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns JSX with at least two heading elements that introduce the memoization demonstration.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a fragment or div with an <h1> and an <h2> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the basic layout with headings that will frame the memoization demonstration.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both an <h1> and an <h2> element in your JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you replaced 'null' with JSX containing heading elements. Remember to use a fragment or wrapper.

steps.title: Add counter controls and input field
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your App component, add a button with the text 'Increment Counter' and an onClick handler that calls incrementCounter. Then add an input field with type='text', value bound to inputValue, and an onChange handler that calls handleInputChange.
steps.hint: Place these elements after the headings you added earlier. The button should trigger the counter increment, and the input should update the inputValue state.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have interactive elements: a button to increment the counter and an input field that updates the inputValue state when typed into.
successCriteria: Button with text 'Increment Counter' and onClick={incrementCounter}
Input field with type='text', value={inputValue}, and onChange={handleInputChange}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the interactive controls that will trigger re-renders and demonstrate memoization behavior.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but make sure both the button and input field are present with the correct attributes and handlers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The required interactive elements are missing or incorrect. Check that you've added both a button and an input field with the specified properties.

steps.title: Display calculation results and performance comparison
steps.instruction: Add two paragraphs below the existing headings to display both the memoized calculation result and the non-memoized calculation result.
steps.hint:
Create two

elements: one showing memoizedResult and another showing expensiveCalculation(counter) directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show two new lines: one displaying the memoized calculation result and another displaying the non-memoized calculation result, allowing comparison.
successCriteria:
Two

elements are added: one showing memoizedResult and another showing expensiveCalculation(counter).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added both calculation results to the UI, making the performance difference visible.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some result display, but make sure to include both the memoized and non-memoized calculations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculation results aren't displayed correctly. Add two paragraphs showing memoizedResult and expensiveCalculation(counter).

steps.title: Add buttons to demonstrate function memoization
steps.instruction: Add two buttons inside the div: one that calls memoizedCallback when clicked, and another that calls nonMemoizedCallback when clicked. Label them appropriately to show which is memoized.
steps.hint: Use the onClick prop on button elements to call the respective callback functions. Place the buttons after the existing paragraphs.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two buttons appear in the UI: one labeled for the memoized callback and one for the non-memoized callback, each with appropriate click handlers.
successCriteria: Two button elements are added with onClick handlers calling memoizedCallback and nonMemoizedCallback respectively, with clear labels.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added buttons to demonstrate the difference between memoized and non-memoized function references. This completes the demo.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added at least one button, but make sure to include both buttons with the correct onClick handlers and labels.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not correctly wired. Add two buttons with onClick handlers for memoizedCallback and nonMemoizedCallback.
